contract: §390 (spec 0069 D2, D5). The fold every link name and link-target key goes through: NFC, then lowercase, then NFC. The tests of Rust `index::normalizer::fold_name` read this file; the frontend's `foldName` tests are to read it too (the frontend PR). `checks` names what a case is there to catch, and a reader asserts it: `input-not-nfc` - the input is not in NFC, so a fold without NFC gives another key; `final-nfc` - NFC then lowercase alone gives another key, so the last NFC is load-bearing. Every character outside ASCII is written as a JSON unicode escape, so that no editor or copy recomposes it. The folded values were computed with Node 24.21 `s.normalize('NFC').toLowerCase().normalize('NFC')` (2026-10-06); the Rust test is a second implementation. The FIRST NFC changed no key in a search over every code point and every uppercase or titlecase letter followed by one mark from U+0300-U+036F or six others (Node 24.21, 2026-10-06), so no case here can show it.

cases.why: a path is folded whole, its separators kept
Korean typed on a keyboard (NFC) is its own key
the same name stored decomposed (NFD) folds to the typed one
a decomposed path folds to the composed path
precomposed capital E-acute lowercases to precomposed e-acute
decomposed capital E-acute folds to the key of the precomposed spelling
no precomposed capital J-caron: lowercase gives j + caron, and only the last NFC composes it to U+01F0
no precomposed capital H-macron-below: only the last NFC composes h + U+0331 to U+1E96
capital I-dot lowercases to i + U+0307, and the last NFC orders the mark below ahead of it
capital I-dot has no one-letter lowercase: i + combining dot above
capital sharp s lowercases to U+00DF
the Kelvin sign: NFC makes it K and lowercase alone makes it k, so the key is k either way
Greek capital sigma at the end lowercases to final sigma
before the dot and a letter it is not final: fold strings of one shape, the extension already off
